cards.text: DELPHINE B-ROLL — PACKING EXPANSION (10 SCENES)

cards.title: CONCEPT
cards.text: v5 — ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND DESIGNED OUT. Four rounds of prompt-hardening failed because the problem was never the wording: our own product truth already documents that this flap and lock survive at MEDIUM distance and shatter in MACRO, and all 8 open frames were macro shots of the bag's mouth filling the frame. Inspected at 2x magnification, every frame had invented a different flap silhouette and cutout pattern. The fix is shot design, not prompt language: the folded-back flap is now either CROPPED OUT of frame (tight inserts on hands, mouth rim and contents — which is what real packing UGC actually looks like) or the bag is CLOSED and shot at medium distance, where the mechanism renders correctly every time. Result: zero invented flap geometry anywhere in the set, and the inserts are stronger packing b-roll than the wide open-bag shots were. On approval these join stills/ as 059-068 and get Omni-animated (061 OVERHEAD, 062/063 HOLD, rest HANDS).

cards.text: NOTES

cards.title: The actual root cause
cards.text: PRODUCT-TRUTH already recorded that this flap and turn lock survive at medium distance and shatter in macro (same failure as the Weekender flap). Every open frame in v1-v4 was a macro of the mouth. Prompt hardening cannot beat a known-broken distance regime; the shot has to change. Inspected at 2x, v4 frames showed a different invented flap silhouette and cutout count in every single frame.

cards.title: New standing rule
cards.text: Delphine open-bag b-roll: either crop the flap out of frame (tight insert on hands/mouth/contents) or shoot the bag CLOSED at medium distance. Never render the folded-back flap large in frame. This matches real packing UGC anyway — hands and contents, not bag portraits.

cards.title: Spend
